A checkout ingestion graph supplies validated JSON baskets to one Normalizer. The next writer stores children keyed by source-row identity and ordinal. Parent monetary and calendar fields have already been typed by the reader; unknown JSON properties are harmless. The component must retain the business context without interpreting optional absence as a reused value.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. Flatten the basket JSON into child-table rows. A nonblank payload has an object root whose lines member is either missing, null or an array; null, empty and whitespace-only payloads, missing lines, null lines and an empty array each produce no children.
2. Array elements are objects with a required nonblank sku string. Preserve its exact spelling, internal and surrounding whitespace as child_code; repeated codes remain separate children. Parent references may repeat and must never be used as a cache key.
3. Assign ordinal from the original one-based array position, beginning with 1 and ending at the array length. Parents arrive in source order and all children of one parent precede the next parent’s children; no sorting or duplicate removal is permitted.
4. An optional details member is missing, null or an object. Its optional note is missing, null or a string. Missing/null details or note yields child_note null; an explicitly empty note stays empty, and every other note retains whitespace unchanged.

Equipment channels are ordered by map key

A factory receives telemetry objects with dynamically named channels rather than a fixed sensor array. The Normalizer fans each envelope into an observation relation consumed by maintenance analytics. The schema validator guarantees object shapes and property types, but device firmware may still send bad numeric text. Disabled channels are intentionally opaque and should never trigger parsing failures.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. The equipment payload is either null/blank or a JSON object with optional channels, itself missing, null or an object keyed by channel names. Empty envelopes and absent/null/empty channel maps produce zero observations. Each channel value is a non-null object and its key is a nonempty ASCII string.
2. Visit keys in ascending case-sensitive lexical order, independently of JSON property insertion order. position is the one-based position in this sorted list of all channel keys. A suppressed channel still occupies its position, so emitted positions may have gaps.
3. A channel has optional enabled, which is boolean or null. Only an explicit false suppresses the channel; missing and null enabled mean enabled. Suppressed entries may contain arbitrary malformed value text and must be discarded before reading or parsing that text.
4. For enabled entries the optional value is null, missing or a string. Missing/null/trimmed-empty becomes reading_value null and quality_cd MISSING. Distinguish genuine zero from missing and preserve a signed valid decimal exactly at two output places.
5. A nonblank value is valid only when its trimmed text matches an optional minus, one through six digits, and optionally a dot followed by one or two digits. Otherwise still emit the observation with null reading_value and quality_cd BAD_TEXT. Valid numeric text produces quality_cd GOOD; no conversion error may abort this graph.
6. The exact channel name is copied, without uppercasing. Metadata context including rated_capacity, commissioned_on, machine_note and machine_unused_archive accompanies each enabled entry; omit only channels_json from the child record.
7. Each equipment envelope starts with a new map and key list. Repeated machine_key values refer to separate measurements. A missing map after a populated map must produce no stale observations; a singleton map emits position 1 even on the final parent.

Overdue payment routing bypasses irrelevant amount defects

A payment operations graph uses this Partition to feed terminal, held, overdue, review, routine and defect queues. A separate Reformat on the defect branch derives the reason; all Partition edges retain the full source record. Credit controllers care about old invoices before value-based review, so a defect in a lower-priority attribute must not displace a business decision already made.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. Six connected payment queues share the input metadata: 0 terminal, 1 manual hold, 2 overdue, 3 high value, 4 ordinary, and 5 defective text. Each row reaches exactly one queue. Apply the following rules in their numbered priority, preserving arrival order within each queue.
2. An exact REVERSED status wins queue 0, then hold_flag true wins queue 1. Neither branch examines amount_txt or invoice_day_txt. Status null, empty, different case and surrounding spaces do not qualify as terminal.
3. Only remaining rows inspect invoice_day_txt. Null, empty or whitespace-only means unknown invoice date. Otherwise trim, require exactly yyyy-MM-dd with two-digit month/day, and verify a real calendar date in UTC. Impossible dates and differently shaped dates go to defective queue 5, even when an amount or priority would otherwise qualify.
4. For a valid known invoice date, overdue means strictly before 2026-01-01. Such a row wins queue 2 without reading its amount, including malformed amount text. January 1 itself is not overdue; unknown invoice dates are not overdue.
5. After the preceding checks, trim amount_txt. Null/blank means zero. A nonblank value must have an optional leading minus, at most six integer digits, and optionally one or two fractional digits. Any other shape, excessive precision or invalid text goes to queue 5, including urgent rows.
6. A successfully interpreted amount at least 10000 wins queue 3. Negative values never qualify. Other rows use queue 4, except an exact URGENT priority combined with a strictly positive amount also wins queue 3. Empty/null priority and zero/negative urgent amounts remain ordinary.
7. Unexpected errors while evaluating a row must be logged and routed to queue 5. Invalid business text may be classified explicitly or by a logged error path; neither silent dropping nor component abortion is allowed. The downstream defect Reformat obtains its reason from its own validation and does not need this Partition to add fields.
8. Every edge carries the original record, including raw strings, nullable due_at and insured_value. No output construction, input edits or cross-row state is needed. Duplicate payment identifiers, the initial terminal row and the last urgent row must all survive exactly once.

A refrigerated carrier streams observations to a stateful Partition. The graph guarantees contiguous trips and numeric sample ordering, but disabled devices and malformed readings remain in the stream for operational accounting. Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. A refrigeration monitor routes each sample unchanged to one of five queues: 0 disabled sensors, 1 faulty measurement text, 2 missing samples, 3 alarm and 4 normal. Samples are sorted into contiguous trip_id groups and increasing sample_no; duplicate numbers are allowed and keep their arrival order. Upstream validation guarantees sample_no is an integer from 0 through 1000000000, so gaps are measured within that bounded counter domain.
2. The first record of each trip establishes fresh state: there is no previous valid temperature or sample number. Trip IDs are exact case-sensitive text. Use an explicit seen-valid flag because zero degrees and sample number zero are valid baseline values, not missing sentinels.
3. sensor_off true routes to queue 0 without inspecting temperature_txt. Disabled rows do not update the previous-valid baseline, even when their supplied temperature is well formed or the sample number is far ahead.

test.user_message:
Claims audit keeps history only for accepted requests

An insurer’s audit Reformat reads its run configuration from typed graph dictionary entries. It receives every claim, including records that opted out, and appends audit decisions without changing source attributes. The accepted sequence and monetary total belong only to this component execution, rather than an external sequence. Disabled auditing must be safe even when a timestamp or the otherwise unused cutoff text is malformed.

Write the complete CTL2 for this component only, including its required entry functions.

1. The graph dictionary supplies auditEnabled boolean true, auditLabel string CLAIMS-R2, and cutoffText string 2026-01-01 00:00:00. These entries may change between runs. Dictionary auditEnabled is the run-level switch, while audit_requested is each row’s request; neither substitutes for the other.
2. If auditing is disabled for the run or not requested by this row, emit audit_state BYPASS, audit_label null, accepted_at null, accepted_index zero, accepted_running equal to the current accepted monetary total, and previous_claim_key null. Do not inspect submitted_txt or parse cutoffText on this branch.
3. For a requested enabled row, submitted_txt must be present and match exactly yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss before strict UTC calendar parsing. Null, blank, impossible dates and different shapes yield audit_state BAD_TIME, null accepted_at and previous_claim_key, index zero and the unchanged running total. These are ordinary output records, not thrown errors.
4. Parse dictionary cutoffText strictly in UTC only when a row reaches valid submission-time evaluation. It is guaranteed valid when auditing is enabled. A submitted timestamp before the cutoff yields audit_state TOO_OLD with the same nonaccepted outputs as BAD_TIME; equality is accepted.
5. An accepted row emits audit_state ACCEPTED and its parsed submitted time into accepted_at. accepted_index counts only accepted records, one-based across the whole stream. Rejected/bypassed rows do not consume an index or advance accepted-history state.
6. claimed_amount may be null, zero or negative within +/-1000000; null contributes zero to the accepted running total. Add the current accepted amount before emitting accepted_running. For every nonaccepted row preserve the total already accumulated, including when it is zero.
7. previous_claim_key is null on the first accepted record; otherwise it is the exact claim_key from the immediately preceding accepted record, skipping all intervening nonaccepted rows. Empty claim_key is allowed and must be remembered as a valid prior key. Use explicit accepted-history state, not null testing a default string/date.
8. audit_label equals the current dictionary label on enabled/requested rows, including BAD_TIME and TOO_OLD, but remains null on bypasses. Copy every original claim field unchanged; emit every source row in arrival order, retain duplicates and do not reorder claims by parsed timestamp.
9. A new component execution starts accepted index and monetary total at zero with no preceding accepted key. Dictionary entries are read-only configuration and must never be mutated to store counters. Unexpected errors after business guards must fail visibly or log before propagating; no silent skipping is permitted.
